Many Chinese women are still hesitant to stand up for themselves. This is hardly a new issue, but was problematized a century ago in stories by Chinese luminaries Lu Xun and Qiu Jin. 

Essay on intersections of literature and #MeToo by @SinophileMatson: https://t.co/wY8vqojnbh

I collated this from suggestions from @NuVoices  members. Ways to take action to support anti-racism and practice Black solidarity in your daily lives, especially if you work in the fields of #China journalism, research, academic, events. https://t.co/id91R7o15c #BlackLivesMatter

A simple but important thing journalists, academics and event organizers can do is regularly feature Black voices and perspectives on the greater #China region. Open directory of experts by @blkvoiceonchina https://t.co/zDMsF7sVoS #BlackLivesMatter

Looking forward to participating in this discussion next Thursday. Register now to join us --  Why is racism deeply rooted in Canada, and what are some solutions? @juniedesil @ufvran, @poeticjfdn, @sharnftc, @joannachiu, @JagdeeshMann, @modhaliwal https://t.co/2kFICpnLHX #BLM

Event poster. Feel free to pass on to anyone who'd like to join. Some extremely thoughtful speakers on the panel I'm excited to learn from. @juniedesil @ufvran, @poeticjfdn, @sharnftc, @joannachiu, @JagdeeshMann, @modhaliwal #BlackLivesMatter #cdnpoli https://t.co/gP4uoWh010

Back in March, myself and @_laujessie @yskevinhuang @rzhongnotes wrote about anti-Asian #COVID19 racism around the world. What the #BlackLivesMatter movement now shows is that it's time for allies to step up. POC have told our stories over and over again. https://t.co/HWsylSFc5E

With #BlackLivesMatter, we're in a critical moment in time, where there is no excuse for silence in the face of  institutional racism. Reading the testimonials about @columbiajourn in this letter, I realized that my experiences weren't unique to my year. https://t.co/eZKY0cuuVL

For me, my instinct was to hit the books to study how to be more anti-racist. 

Then I realized that part of the problem was that I was always over-working and didn't leave time to reflect on uncomfortable truths and try to understand. https://t.co/ktUfvgKWQF #BlackLivesMatter

And images can be more powerful than words. Here's a photo essay by @dong_mengyu, who told me she embarked on this project to counter the misinformation about #blacklivesmatter on Chinese social media: https://t.co/LST9DniBaO

Lots to think about. I wonder if the #MeToo and #BlackLivesMatter and anti-racism movements will intersect. Or if intersectionality will be more widely understood. It’s hard to get through life unscathed without certain privileges that provide greater safety and opportunities.
